title: Why your Wi-Fi is slower in the kitchen

segments.text: Why is your Wi-Fi slower in the kitchen?
Often, it's your microwave. It uses the same radio band as your Wi-Fi.
Step one: Wi-Fi sends data as radio waves, often on the two point four gigahertz band.
Step two: a microwave heats food with radio waves too, at two point four five gigahertz, right inside that band.
Step three, the surprise: the metal box keeps almost all of it in, but a little gets out.
And your microwave makes around a thousand watts. Your router sends with one watt, at most.
So even that little leak can drown out your Wi-Fi while it runs.
The fix: use your router's five gigahertz band, far away from the microwave's frequency.
